requests.what: Add a rich array of small round bass and chord buttons across the bass panel: three staggered columns, alternating PEARL, PEARL_GREEN, and PEARL_PINK caps, each with a tiny GOLD rim and a dark burgundy shadow.
Place a small Italian filigree medallion centered high on the bellows: a dark burgundy oval backing, a GOLD rim, and a stylized PEARL treble-clef emblem. Keep it shallow and flush to the front.
Add five compact register switches above the piano keys, each as a short ivory slider with a burgundy slot and a tiny GOLD cap. Arrange them in one neat horizontal row.
Add a slim GOLD nameplate on the upper treble casing, with a dark burgundy inset and raised cream lettering reading 'ITALIA'. Use a small rounded plaque, not a floating sign.
Build a decorative bass grille on the upper half of the bass casing: a shallow burgundy inset with six small horizontal GOLD slots and a thin PEARL border, all seated on the shell.
Add four small GOLD bellows corner clips where the burgundy bellows meet the top and bottom rails. Each clip should be a chunky low-poly bracket with a tiny pearl rivet.
Add paired GOLD shoulder-strap buckles at the top shoulders, one on each side of the accordion. They should be squat rectangular buckles with dark leather through their centers.
Add four small GOLD protective studs around the lower corners, two visible on the front and two peeking around the sides. Keep them integrated into the lower rail.
Add a restrained row of tiny GOLD rivets following the outer front frame of both shell casings, with evenly spaced low-poly heads and no rivets across the clear center inlay.

Paint the treble shell as Italian mother-of-pearl: broad angular cream, blush, and mint nacre facets with subtle ivory highlights, a restrained burgundy border shadow, and a clean clear center for the nameplate.
Paint the bass shell with a rich mother-of-pearl mosaic using PEARL, PEARL_GREEN, and PEARL_PINK, arranged as large radial fan facets around the button field while preserving the GOLD frame.
Texture the bellows face as alternating deep burgundy leather folds with slightly lighter wine-red ridges, subtle vertical grain, and a soft worn highlight on the forward-facing pleats.
Give the keyboard surround a restrained warm ivory nacre texture with faint pink-green mother-of-pearl shimmer, leaving every white and black piano key crisp and readable.

Paint the right wing membrane with alternating TURQUOISE and DEEP_TEAL feather panels, thin GOLD ribs, and small MAGENTA diamond marks arranged like carved folk ornament.

Add a coin-door badge and fittings: a small gold octagonal token emblem, two cyan coin return slots, a magenta service light, and four silver corner rivets.

Add a recessed CRT screen treatment: a thin violet inner rim, three subtle cyan scanline strips, and a small magenta reflection diamond in the upper corner. Keep the center of the screen mostly clear.

Add a short coiled power cable emerging from the rear lower panel, using BLACK, VIOLET, and CYAN bands, plus a small rectangular strain-relief block. Keep it close to the cabinet footprint.

Paint the CRT screen with a dark NAVY-to-PURPLE glass field, a soft CYAN horizon glow, sparse MAGENTA pixel sparks, and restrained horizontal scanlines. Keep it readable as a blank screen behind the added reflection.

Paint the left side panel with a bold 1980s synthwave composition: BLACK and NAVY base, a large hot-pink sunset disk low toward the rear, cyan perspective grid lines, and a few angular violet speed streaks. Keep the outer neon rail unobscured.
Paint the right side panel to match the left: BLACK and NAVY base, MAGENTA sunset disk, CYAN horizon grid, and VIOLET geometric streaks, mirrored in spirit but not mechanically copied.

Paint the control deck with a dark PURPLE surface, a cyan perimeter pinstripe, small magenta directional arrows, and a sparse checker motif around the controls. Do not cover the joystick and button clearances.

requests.what: Neon weather light bar across the cab roof: a slim dark housing, six chunky lamps alternating CYAN and MAGENTA, and two metal brackets. Keep it graphic and high-contrast.
Paint the clear sign board with a bold cream arctic research emblem and the words POLAR STATION in block lettering, using SNOW_LIGHT, YELLOW, and INK.
Add a satellite dish feed assembly: a slim arm, a small receiver pod, and two little braces in METAL_LIGHT, with one CYAN indicator.
Build a crisp antenna crown on the mast: three different-length whip antennas, a crossbar, small insulators, and a red warning pennant. Use METAL, METAL_DARK, RED, and YELLOW.
Add a bundled exterior communications cable running from the rear side of the cabin toward the mast, with three square cable clips and a small junction box.
Add a bright yellow hazard stencil and two dark bands to the pair of fuel drums. Keep the lettering abstract and graphic, not realistic.
Lay a clean six-by-four grid of pale blue solar cells into the two angled panels, with a dark perimeter frame and two bright corner glints.
Fill the orange cargo sled with three strapped expedition cases, a rolled orange tarp, and two pale snow hooks. Use CRATE, CRATE_LIGHT, ORANGE, and METAL.
Place a short striped snow marker pole at the front corner, with alternating RED and SNOW_LIGHT bands and a tiny triangular flag.

Paint a restrained Firewatch-style geometric weathering pattern on the left hull side: broad HULL_LIGHT and HULL_DARK diagonal blocks, with a few SNOW_BLUE frost streaks. Keep the windows and trim clear.
Paint the right hull side with offset HULL and HULL_DARK field patches and a faded cream unit number near the rear, leaving the cable route readable.
Add graphic snow streaks and wind-scoured bands to both roof planes using SNOW_LIGHT, SNOW_BLUE, and ROOF_LIGHT. Keep the roof light bar mounting strip plain.
Give the solar panels a crisp alternating PANEL and PANEL_DARK cell pattern with thin ICE highlights and a subtle diagonal reflection.

Mirror the left gill detail on the right side: a dense but readable fan of rounded branching filaments and little leaf frills in GILL, GILL_LIGHT and GILL_HIGHLIGHT. Keep the filaments separated and puppet-like.

Place a small symmetrical constellation of dark pink freckles across the cream muzzle, with three to five rounded dots per side and two tiny freckles near the nose. Keep clear space around both eyes and the smile.

Enhance both large eyes with layered glossy highlights: one large white rounded glint, one tiny pink-white glint, and a subtle dark upper lid rim. The eyes should remain nearly black and very readable from the front.
Add soft round toe pads to all four feet: three tiny cream-pink pads on each paw, arranged in a simple chibi fan and seated directly on the existing toes. Use PAW with small BELLY highlights.

Add a row of broad, dark-pink fin rays inside the tail fin, following its length from the rump toward the pointed tip. Use six or seven low-poly tapered rods, evenly spaced, with slightly brighter tips.

Add two soft stylized blush patches on the cheeks, one on each side just below and outside the eyes. Use BLUSH as flat low-poly discs or tiny clustered spheres, clearly visible but not covering the smile.
Add small pale cream collar bands where each of the six gill stalks emerges from the head. The bands should be chunky, clean, and slightly lighter than the belly, like little ornamental cuffs.
Add a few oversized rounded axolotl speckles along the upper back and rear flanks, using BODY_SHADOW and BODY_LIGHT. Keep the belly clear and leave the central back surface open for the texture pass.

Paint a restrained hand-painted pastel pattern over the body: mostly BODY with irregular soft BODY_LIGHT patches and a warm BELLY underside. Use broad low-frequency patches rather than noise, keeping the silhouette and the clean chibi material readable.

Paint the head with a gentle BODY to BODY_LIGHT gradient, a warm BELLY muzzle transition, and very subtle rosy cheek variation. Do not texture over the eyes, mouth, or gills; those should remain crisp separate parts.

Paint the tail fin with a translucent-looking flat-color gradient from TAIL_FIN at the root to GILL_LIGHT near the tip, plus a narrow BODY_SHADOW edge. Keep the fin graphic and low-poly, not realistic.

subject: babaYagaHut
pitch:
Category: Diorama.
Subject: Baba Yaga's hut on chicken legs.
Style: Slavic folk art.

requests.what: A large protective Slavic sun talisman on the front door: dark iron outline, warm gold center, eight alternating red and cream rays, and two small hanging bells. Keep it bold and folk-carved.
A pair of chunky blue-green wooden shutters around the left-side window, each with red diamond paint, black hinges, and a gold crescent clasp.
A pair of chunky blue-green wooden shutters around the right-side window, each with red diamond paint, black hinges, and a gold crescent clasp. Mirror the opposite side.

A carved witch-hut finial at the roof ridge: a little dark wooden pole, a stylized golden sun disk, and two curled red folk-art leaves. It should break the silhouette clearly without covering the chimney.
Three bundles of dried herbs and red berries hanging beneath the front eave on short cords, with green leaves, ochre stems, and small cream seed beads.
A tiny folk bone wind chime under the opposite eave: a dark carved crossbar, three pale bone pieces, red thread, and a little blue bead. Keep it inside the hut silhouette.
A crooked witch's broom tied against the hut side: bent brown handle, bundled yellow bristles, red binding cord, and a few blue folk-painted bands.
Matching carved wooden ankle spurs on both chicken legs: small ochre side plates, red cords, and two blunt cream spikes per ankle. Follow the existing leg bones and keep the feet planted.
Paint the roof shingles with broad Slavic folk-art chevrons and small sun symbols in ROOF_LIGHT, GABLE_LIGHT, RED, and BERRY. Keep the main roof dark and leave the ridge beam plain.
Mirror the hand-painted Slavic chevron and sun-symbol pattern from the opposite roof slope, with slightly uneven brush edges and a few darker weathered shingles.
Add a wide painted folk border around the front wall in TEAL, CREAM, RED, and WOOD_GOLD: repeating diamonds, little rosettes, and a thin dark outline. Do not cover the door or gable.
Paint the door with vertical rough wood grain in WOOD_DARK and WOOD, a faded red border, and three small cream carved marks. Keep the center clear for the talisman.
Paint both chicken legs with chunky alternating LEG_GOLD and LEG_DARK scale bands, a few red folk diamonds around the knees, and pale highlights on the forward-facing facets.

A layered open mouth at the end of the snout: deep NIGHT interior, a thin VERMILION lower lip, two small IVORY tooth glints, and a dark woodblock contour. Follow the existing jaw hinge.
Three tiny OCHRE and VERMILION cord bands wrapped around the visible tusk, with an INK knot. Keep the bands narrow and seated on the ivory.
A thin PALE_BLUE dream ribbon emerging from the snout and curling upward once, like a Japanese painted cloud. Add an INK edge, one TEAL bead, and a small GOLD charm at its tip.
A large flat ukiyo-e dream seal on the upper back: an INK oval border, a vermilion stylized cloud glyph, and two CREAM registration marks. Keep the surrounding indigo back clear.
A pair of simple ear ornaments: small GOLD diamond plates with VERMILION cords, mirrored on both ears and attached near the lower outer ear.
Three narrow VERMILION and CREAM ribbon strips threaded through the dorsal mane, with little square ends. They should follow the creature's spine and read as carved print shapes.
A tiny GOLD bell and PALE_BLUE tassel at the tail tuft, outlined in INK. The bell is ornamental, not metallic-realistic, and must stay within the tail silhouette.
Four small hoof seals, one on each planted foot: CREAM rectangular plaques with a single INK cloud mark and a VERMILION lower edge. Keep them low and flush to the hoof tops.
Two suspended PALE_BLUE spirit beads along the left vapor wisp, each with a tiny GOLD core and a crisp INK rim. They should be sparse and graphic rather than glittery.

A restrained ukiyo-e woodblock texture: broad uneven indigo hatch marks following the body length, slightly lighter CREAM belly brushwork, and a few sparse OCHRE flecks on the rump. Keep the silhouette flat and avoid photoreal fur.

Flat carved-print shading on the head: DEEP_INDIGO contour hatching beneath the brow and cheeks, CREAM block shading around the muzzle, and a few short INK strokes that emphasize the tapir's heavy brow.
Ukiyo-e ear print marks in VERMILION, OCHRE, and INK: two broad interior wedge shapes and three short parallel cut lines, leaving the outer INDIGO rim clean. Mirror the design on earR.
Short alternating OCHRE and CREAM block bands across the tail tuft, with a dark INK contour at the tip and a subtle PALE_BLUE spirit haze around the last segment.

requests.what: Heavy brutalist entrance canopy in raw CONCRETE_DARK: a deep rectangular slab, two angled concrete brackets, a recessed warm wall lamp, and a small engraved housing-block number in CHALK. Keep the assembly chunky and architectural.
Recessed communal entry doors at the central front portal: paired dark glass doors in WINDOW, a thick CONCRETE_LIGHT frame, four narrow vertical handles in METAL, and a shallow threshold step.

Raw brutalist balcony guards on the three front balconies: thick precast parapet panels in CONCRETE_LIGHT, narrow repetitive rectangular cut-outs, dark shadow gaps, and four oversized METAL drain scuppers.

A row of deep vertical brise-soleil screens across the upper cantilever facade, built from alternating CONCRETE_LIGHT fins and dark voids. Use a severe repeating rhythm and leave the window openings readable behind them.
A slim architectural light bar along the front roof coping: a dark METAL housing, six alternating CYAN and MAGENTA lamps, two concrete brackets, and a small cable disappearing into the roof.
A dense rooftop mechanical vent cluster in CONCRETE_DARK and METAL: three square exhaust housings, two short polygonal ducts, louver slats, and a few exposed dark cables. Keep it low and blocky.
A squat rooftop water tank assembly behind the stair tower: faceted cylindrical tank in CONCRETE_LIGHT, dark METAL bands, four short support legs, a blocky access hatch, and one thin overflow pipe.

External emergency stair on the building's left side: two zig-zagging raw concrete flights, thick landing boxes, dark METAL handrails, and a red emergency placard. The stair must hug the side wall and remain visibly secondary to the block.
A narrow rear access bridge in CONCRETE_DARK connecting the central stair tower to the rear apartments, with two heavy side parapets, a recessed doorway, and a single METAL service light.

Minimal rooftop antenna array in METAL: one square mast, three unequal horizontal rods, two small dish-like plates, and four tension cables anchored to the concrete roof. Keep the silhouette sparse and graphic.

Paint the exposed front concrete in CONCRETE, CONCRETE_LIGHT, and CONCRETE_DARK as raw poured concrete: broad formwork panels, irregular vertical water stains, subtle aggregate mottling, darker recesses under every slab, and a few restrained repaired-patch rectangles. Do not texture the dark windows.

Paint both side masses in CONCRETE and CONCRETE_DARK with large horizontal form-tie bands, vertical runoff streaks below window heads, chipped-looking tonal patches, and a slightly darker lower metre near the plinth.

Paint the projecting upper volume with pale CONCRETE_LIGHT top planes, mid-tone CONCRETE wall planes, and hard CONCRETE_SHADOW seams beneath the cantilever. Add a sparse grid of panel joints aligned with the upper windows.

Paint the stair tower and roof coping in weathered CONCRETE_LIGHT and CONCRETE_DARK, with dark damp marks at the base, broad slab-edge bands, small aggregate flecks, and clean clear areas reserved for the roof equipment.

requests.what: A cheerful robot light bar on the helmet roof: a thin cardboard housing, six glowing lamps alternating CYAN and MAGENTA, two folded mounting brackets, and tiny dark wiring. Keep it playful and handmade.

Two oversized friendly robot eyes on the front screen, made from rounded lens frames with bright WHITE highlights, CYAN irises, and dark pupils. Leave a little space between them and keep them readable from the front.

A small smiling speaker grille across the lower face: a dark rounded rectangular plate, five short pale slots, and two tiny corner bolts. It should feel like a kid's robot costume rather than a military machine.
A bold handmade robot emblem centered on the chest: a dark outlined badge with a bright YELLOW lightning-bolt star, two little rivets, and a short cardboard nameplate beneath it.
Large cardboard shoulder bolt assemblies on both shoulders: concentric octagonal plates, one pale highlight wedge, and a dark centre cap on each side. Mirror the pair.
A pair of chunky exposed costume cables running from each shoulder toward the wrists, with three dark cable bands and small yellow cardboard cable clips. Mirror them on both arms.
Friendly mitten-like robot hands with three short cardboard finger blocks and one thumb block per hand. Use warm cardboard, dark separation seams, and no sharp weapon-like points.
Large octagonal knee plates on both legs with dark outlines, warm gold centres, and two cardboard rivets each. Mirror the plates and keep the lower leg silhouette clear.
Simple chunky boot tread details: three broad dark rubber strips across each cardboard foot, with a small yellow heel marker. Mirror both feet and keep the soles flat on the floor.
Two harmless cardboard exhaust stacks peeking from behind the torso, each with a dark opening, a folded rim, and one short dangling cable. They are costume decorations, not flames.

Subtle cardboard craft texture across the torso: broad warm kraft-paper fibres, faint horizontal corrugation lines, slightly darker fold shadows at the edges, and a few soft scuffed patches. Keep the chest emblem panel mostly calm and readable.

Warm kraft cardboard texture on the helmet shell: broad paper fibres, slightly lighter top-facing faces, darker side folds, and a few irregular handmade tape marks. Keep the front screen border plain and crisp.

Hand-painted cardboard side markings in CARDBOARD_GOLD and EDGE: two wide diagonal caution bands, a tiny faded unit number near the rear, and a few worn pencil construction marks. Mirror the pattern on hullSideR.
Small-scale cardboard fibre texture on both forearms and upper arms, with darker folded seams around the elbow and a few pale tape patches. Keep the cable request area visible above the texture.

Add a matching but slightly smaller horn crown to the hydra's right outer head, with two broken-looking BONE horns, dark bronze collars, and tiny red war-paint cuts.
Hang heavy bronze-and-iron chain ornaments down the front of all five throats. Each chain should have chunky links, a few pointed studs, and a dark red leather tie disappearing into the scales.
Build a massive layered bronze shoulder pauldron on the hydra's left side: three overlapping plates, sharp lower teeth, dark seams, and large GOLD rivets. Keep it clear of the neck root.
Build a massive layered bronze shoulder pauldron on the hydra's right side: three overlapping plates, sharp lower teeth, dark seams, and large GOLD rivets. Keep it clear of the neck root.

At the tail's upper curve, add a small ancient bronze reliquary plate with a glowing-looking amber inset, four rivets, and a short BONE spike on each side.
Give every foot three thick CLAW talons with dark bronze nail guards and narrow red leather bands around the ankle. Repeat the same brutal motif on all four feet.

Build a deep ember-red glow assembly inside all five mouths: a faceted ember core, two smaller side sparks, and thin dark smoke-like spikes tucked behind the teeth. The glow must remain inside the open jaws.

Paint the main torso with large overlapping SCALE plates in SCALE, SCALE_LIGHT, and SCALE_HIGHLIGHT. Put BELLY and BELLY_LIGHT on the underside, with a subtle irregular transition and a few SCAR-red scratches near the shoulder.

Paint all five necks with broad armor-like scales: dark SCALE on the backs, SCALE_LIGHT on raised edges, and a continuous BELLY strip on the front of each throat. Keep the pattern bold and readable at a distance.
Paint the five skulls with charcoal SCALE and warm SCALE_LIGHT planes, then add angular SCAR-red war-paint slashes around the brows and cheek plates. Leave the eyes, teeth, horns, and mouths clean.
Texture both shoulder pauldrons as battered BRONZE armor with BRONZE_LIGHT bevels, dark IRON seams, worn GOLD rivets, and a few small SCAR-red paint marks.

requests.what: Build a deep rectangular stainless sink basin inset into the counter, with a thick rim, dark drain, angular faucet and two short hot/cold handles. Use STEEL, STEEL_DARK, BLACK and RUST; keep it heavy, utilitarian and visibly recessed.

Add a compact industrial galley range on the clear right side of the back counter: two dark burner plates, raised square pot supports, a small control rail and four red and amber indicator buttons. Use BLACK, STEEL_DARK, STEEL, RED and AMBER.

Build an exposed ceiling light bar across the galley: a slim dark housing, six chunky lamps alternating CYAN and MAGENTA, two metal suspension brackets and a few black cable loops. The lamps should feel like retro-futurist fluorescent emergency hardware.

Add a compact Nostromo control panel on the rear wall, with a thick bevelled housing, three horizontal dark display windows, vertical toggle banks, red warning lamps and one small amber status display. Use HULL_DARK, BLACK, STEEL, RED and AMBER. Keep it rectangular and tactile, not sleek.

Add a magnetic utensil rail above the counter with four hanging angular tools: a ladle, a spatula, a long knife and a hook. Use STEEL, STEEL_DARK, RUST and BLACK, with chunky silhouettes and visible mounting collars.

Build a rear-wall ventilation bank in the reserved left section: a raised rectangular frame, six deep black slots, a central mesh-like grille made from thick bars and two rusted fastener plates. Use HULL_DARK, BLACK, STEEL_DARK and RUST.

Add a bundled cable loom down the right bulkhead, held by four metal clamps. Use three parallel thick cables in BLACK, RUST and STEEL_DARK, with a few angled bends so the bundle feels installed rather than decorative.

Add a small bolted warning placard on the left wall with an inset ochre hazard triangle, a red emergency stripe and two rows of tiny raised bars standing in for lettering. Use PANEL_LIGHT, HAZARD, RED, BLACK and STEEL.
Add a small under-cabinet mug rack with a dark horizontal rail, four pale industrial mugs and four short hooks. Use STEEL_DARK, OFF_WHITE, RUST and BLACK. Keep the mugs blocky and visibly suspended.

Paint the rear bulkhead in a restrained worn olive-grey HULL and HULL_DARK industrial panel pattern. Add subtle soot near the counter, faded maintenance blocks and a small stencilled unit number near the upper right, without making it clean or glossy.

Paint the lower cabinet fronts in alternating HULL, HULL_DARK and PANEL sections with chipped edges, grime along the bottom, and faint pale maintenance labels. Preserve the raised frame geometry and keep the overall palette muted.

Add a sparse vertical panel pattern to the left bulkhead using HULL, PANEL and HULL_DARK, with faded rectangular service marks and darker grime in the lower corners. The result should look like painted, repeatedly serviced spacecraft metal.

Paint the overhead locker fronts with uneven HULL and PANEL blocks, black recessed seams, small faded cream labels and a few rust blooms around the hinges. Keep the faces readable and leave all handles visible.

Add a narrow triangular beach pennant at the mast crown, striped alternately in BEACH_ORANGE and SUN_YELLOW, with a short dark cap and a tiny dangling wind ribbon.
Add a small rotating wind vane on the front bulkhead: a horizontal axle, two opposing paddle blades, and a little orange central hub.
At every visible crank wheel, add a dark teal outer cap, a cream washer, and a small orange offset crank pin. Keep the linkage joints readable and leave the wheel faces mostly clear.
Add broad, low-profile sand paddles beneath each of the six feet. They should be rounded rectangular plates in BEACH_ORANGE with dark teal heel bands and two small cream studs per paddle.

Place a sparse row of small orange rivet heads along the sail's upper and lower tube edges, following the triangular outline without cluttering the central sail.
Add a small cream identification plate on the forward upper side of the body, framed in dark teal and marked with a simple three-line orange symbol.

Paint the long body tube with a restrained beach-weathered pattern: warm ivory as the base, pale sand on upward-facing facets, muted blue-grey on the underside, and occasional broad teal maintenance bands near the three crank stations.
Paint the sail as sun-bleached canvas: cream and muted straw panels with a few flat BEACH_ORANGE seam strips, keeping the centre visually open for the wind marks.

Use the same restrained material language on the articulated legs: pale polymer primary tubes, blue-grey shadow links, orange crank accents, and darker underside sections. Preserve the hard faceted Theo Jansen look.
